facts.value: The Bhakti movement swept through Central and Northern India during the 14th–17th centuries under Muslim rule, originally starting in the eighth century in South India (present-day Tamil Nadu and Kerala).

Saints such as Dnyaneshwar, Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, Vallabhacharya, Surdas, Meera Bai, Kabir, Tulsidas, Ravidas, Namdeo, Eknath, Ramdas, Tukaram, and others taught that people could express their overwhelming love for God.
The Kabir Panth is a religious movement based on the teachings of the Indian poet saint Kabir (1398–1518), who sermonised a monotheism denying both Hinduism and Islam.

Guru Nanak Dev Ji (1469–1539) was the founder of Sikhism, known as Sikh Dharm. Sikhism teaches universal brotherhood and recognizes all humans as equal before Waheguru, with emphasis on teachings from the Guru Granth Sahib.
Christianity was believed to be introduced to India by Thomas the Apostle in 52 CE, who proselytised natives known as Saint Thomas Christians.

Islam is the second largest religion in India, with 14.2% of the population or roughly 172 million people identifying as adherents of Islam (2011 census). The estimated number of Muslims in India for 2024 is projected to be around 204,760,392.
Religion populations in India: Hindus - 966,257,353; Muslims - 172,245,158; Christians - 27,819,588; Sikhs - 20,833,116; Buddhists - 8,442,972; Jains - 4,451,753; Others - 1,953,923.
The six religions awarded 'National minority' status in India are Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Jains, Buddhists, and Zoroastrians (Parsis).
